name: Definition: Highway Lane Centered Cruise Behavior
desc:
Maintain steady longitudinal speed and lateral position within the current lane on a highway when no immediate interaction, routing, or tactical maneuver is required. This is the default steady-state driving behavior.
 
Intent
Maintain progress while complying with traffic rules and ensuring dynamic stability.
 
Entry Condition
SDT is in robotic mode.
SDT is on a highway lane segment with valid lane geometry. SDT is driving in a lane with visible lane markings on both sides of the SDT.
Interior lane width is greater than or equal to 3.5 m.
Minimum horizontal radius of curvature is 450 m.

No lead vehicle requiring active following behavior within engagement distance.
No mandatory routing event (exit, merge, lane drop) within the planning horizon.
No higher-priority interaction or fallback behavior is active.
 
Exit Condition
A lead vehicle enters the following engagement range.
A mandatory or discretionary lane change becomes active.
An on-ramp merge, off-ramp exit, or hazard requires behavior transition.
System health degradation requires fallback (includes unclear lane marking/ low confidence in Lane marking perception).
Out of ODD conditions.

name: Definition: Lane Centered Adaptive Follow
desc:
Description
Regulate longitudinal motion to maintain a safe, comfortable, and legally compliant distance behind a lead vehicle traveling in the same lane.
 
Intent
Reduce collision risk while maintaining reasonable traffic flow and compliance with following-distance expectations.
 
Entry Condition
A lead vehicle is detected and tracked in the ego lane with sufficient confidence.

Headway or distance falls below the cruise disengagement threshold.

Ego vehicle remains lane-aligned with the lead vehicle.

Exit Condition
Lead vehicle exits the lane or exceeds disengagement distance.

Ego initiates a lane change or overtake.

Route event or merge/exit behavior becomes active.

Tracking confidence drops below acceptable threshold.

name: Definition: Lane Change/ Overtaking
desc:
Description
Transition laterally to an adjacent lane to improve progress or satisfy routing requirements, including gap assessment, signaling, execution, and stabilization.
 
Intent
Improve progress or satisfy route constraints while maintaining safety, legality, and predictability.
 
Entry Condition
Adjacent lane exists and lane change is permitted.

Discretionary trigger: lead vehicle significantly slower than desired speed.

Mandatory trigger: lane drop, exit preparation, or obstacle ahead.

Adjacent-lane traffic is sufficiently observable for gap assessment.

Exit Condition
Ego vehicle is fully established and stable in the target lane.

Lane change is safely aborted and ego remains in original lane.

Behavior transitions into adaptive follow or lane-centered cruise.

name: Definition: On-Ramp Merge
desc:
Description
Enter highway mainline traffic from an on-ramp by identifying a suitable gap, adjusting speed accordingly, and merging laterally within the merge zone.
 
Intent
Join the highway flow safely, legally and efficiently while minimizing disruption to mainline traffic.
 
Entry Condition
Ego vehicle is on an on-ramp approaching a merge area.

Mainline traffic is detected and tracked with sufficient confidence.

Route requires highway entry.

Ego vehicle is capable of reaching the entry ramp lane within safe bounds.

Exit Condition
Ego vehicle is fully merged and stabilized in the mainline lane (transitions to Lane-Centered Cruise or Adaptive Follow).

Merge is aborted and ego vehicle reaches desired safe state (stops or holds at end of acceleration lane or pulls over to the should if shoulder available).

Emergency maneuver is triggered.

name: Definition: Off-Ramp Exit
desc:
Description
Navigate the ego vehicle from the mainline highway lane into an off-ramp exit lane, following the planned route and executing the lateral transition within the designated exit zone.
 
Intent
Exit the highway safely and predictably, maintaining compliance with lane geometry and speed limits.
 
Entry Condition
Route plan requires the next off-ramp exit.

Ego vehicle is within the pre-exit planning horizon.

Off-ramp entry geometry is detected and confirmed.

Ego vehicle is capable of reaching the exit lane within safe bounds.

Exit Condition
Ego vehicle is fully positioned in the off-ramp lane and decelerating (behavior transitions to urban or surface street behavior).

Exit is missed and a re-route is required.

Emergency maneuver preempts the exit.

name: Definition: Emergency Stop in Lane
desc:
Description
Execute an immediate, controlled deceleration to bring the ego vehicle to a stop within its current travel lane in response to a critical failure or imminent hazard that precludes transitioning to Stop on shoulder.
 
Intent
Bring the vehicle to a safe stop as quickly as practicable while minimizing collision risk.
 
Entry Condition
A critical DDT-F condition requires an immediate stop and shoulder transition is not possible.

A hazard or system failure precludes continued travel.

Exit Condition
Ego vehicle is stopped in lane with hazard lights active.

Ego vehicle resumes travel lane behavior after stopping related condition is cleared.

Another emergency maneuver overrides the controlled stop.

Emergency services or remote operator intervention is signaled.

 
 
 
Link to Behavior Page: 
https://torc.atlassian.net/wiki/pages/resumedraft.action?draftId=2915696704

name: Definition: Controlled Stop on Shoulder
desc:
Description
Execute a controlled, deliberate deceleration and lateral transition to bring the ego vehicle to a stop on the highway shoulder or emergency stopping lane, in response to a planned or reactive need to exit the travel lane safely.
 
Intent
Bring the vehicle to a safe, stable stop outside the travel lane with minimal risk to occupants and other road users.
 
Entry Condition
A DDT-F condition or planned stop event requires the ego to exit the travel lane.

A shoulder or emergency stopping area is available and geometrically valid.

No higher-priority emergency maneuver is active.

Exit Condition
Shoulder or emergency stopping area is blocked or unavailable.

Ego vehicle resumes travel lane behavior after stopping related condition is cleared.

Another emergency maneuver overrides the controlled stop.

name: Maximum SDT Speed
desc: The SDT shall be designed to not exceed 29.05 m/s (65mph)
rationale: This maximum speed is used in the linked assumption to drive safety analyses

name: Stay In Lane - Tractor
desc:
The SDT shall be designed to limit the duration of any point on the tractor extent being at a lateral distance greater than 0 m outside of the interior lane boundaries to a maximum of 2 consecutive seconds WHEN
Clearly defined lane markings are present on both sides of the SDT AND
Lane width is greater than or equal to 3.5 m AND
Lane horizontal radius of curvature is greater than or equal to 450 m AND
No actor within lateral consideration zone with relative lateral distance less than or equal to the Safe Lateral Buffer (0.3m).
rationale:
Driving within the lane boundaries maximizes safety by reducing collision risks (SDT is more predictable to other roadway users and reduces the likelihood of side-swipe or rear end collisions). It also promotes improved traffic flow and better hazard recognition.
 
To satisfy the stakeholder needs, it is necessary to keep all points on the tractor extent inside the lane. Therefore, "tractor extent" is defined to include the mirrors and sensors.
 
For Driver Out, SDT needs to drive within lane 99.9% of the total driving time (assuming 100% robotic). Since this accounts to almost 7hrs of driving, SDT can have cumulative lane departure duration of total 25.2 seconds. Assuming we could have a maximum of 12 events of ~2 seconds each.

name: Stay in Lane - Trailer
desc:
The SDT shall be designed to limit the duration of any point on the trailer extent being at a lateral distance greater than 0 m outside of the interior lane boundaries to a maximum of 2 consecutive seconds WHEN
Clearly defined lane markings are present on both sides of the SDT AND
Lane width is greater than or equal to 3.5 m AND
Lane horizontal radius of curvature is greater than or equal to 450 m AND
No actor within lateral consideration zone with relative lateral distance less than or equal to the Safe Lateral Buffer (0.3m).
rationale:
Driving within the lane boundaries maximizes safety by reducing collision risks (SDT is more predictable to other roadway users and reduces the likelihood of side-swipe or rear end collisions). It also promotes improved traffic flow and better hazard recognition.
 
For Driver Out, SDT needs to drive within lane 99.9% of the total driving time (assuming 100% robotic). Since this accounts to almost 7hrs of driving, SDT can have cumulative lane departure duration of total 25.2 seconds. Assuming we could have a maximum of 12 events of ~2 seconds each.

name: Lane Departure Failure Rate - Tractor
desc: The SDT shall be designed to limit the violations of  Stay in Lane - Tractor to be less than or equal to 0.03 events per mile evaluated over one mission
rationale: For Driver Out, SDT needs to drive within lane 99.9% of the total driving time (assuming 100% robotic). Since this accounts to almost 7hrs of driving (400 miles round trip), SDT can have cumulative lane departure duration of total 25.2 seconds. Assuming we could have a maximum of 12 events of ~2 seconds each. This results in 12 events per 400 miles or 0.03 events per mile.

name: Lane Departure Failure Rate - Trailer
desc: The SDT shall be designed to limit the violations of  Stay In Lane - Trailer to be less than or equal to 0.03 events per mile evaluated over one mission.
rationale: For Driver Out, SDT needs to drive within lane 99.9% of the total driving time (assuming 100% robotic). Since this accounts to almost 7hrs of driving (400 miles round trip), SDT can have cumulative lane departure duration of total 25.2 seconds. Assuming we could have a maximum of 12 events of ~2 seconds each. This results in 12 events per 400 miles or 0.03 events per mile.

name: Maximum Lateral Deviation from Lane - Tractor
desc:
The SDT shall be designed to keep all points on the tractor extent within a lateral distance of 0.3 m outside of the exterior lane boundaries WHEN
Clearly defined lane markings are present on both sides of the SDT AND
Lane width is greater than or equal to 3.5 m AND
Lane horizontal radius of curvature is greater than or equal to 450 m AND
No actor within lateral consideration zone with relative lateral distance less than or equal to the Safe Lateral Buffer (0.3m).
rationale:
The rationale is to bound the max lateral deviation for a lane departure event for two main reasons (in order of priority) - so that we are (1) ensuring safety of other actors and the SDT, and (2) complying with the traffic law. 

Based on the assumptions that an adjacent actor drifts no more than 0.48 m (2 standard deviations) within its lane and that the actor's width is no more than 2.1m, the SDT can leave the ego lane by (3.5 m - 2.1 m)/2 - 0.48 m =0.22 m and still avoid a collision with the adjacent actor. Based on the standards, ISO11270 and UNECE-157, the max deviation permissible is around 0.3-0.4m. Of the different values, we pick a value of 0.3 m as our initial estimate.

name: Maximum Lateral Deviation from Lane - Trailer
desc:

Clearly defined lane markings are present on both sides of the SDT AND
Lane width is greater than or equal to 3.5 m AND
Lane horizontal radius of curvature is greater than or equal to 450 m AND
No actor within lateral consideration zone with relative lateral distance less than or equal to the Safe Lateral Buffer (0.3m).
rationale:
The rationale is to bound the max lateral deviation for a lane departure event for two main reasons (in order of priority) - so that we are (1) ensuring safety of other actors and the SDT, and (2) complying with the traffic law.

Based on the standards, ISO11270 and UNECE-157, the max deviation permissible is around 0.3-0.4m. Of the different values, we pick a value of 0.3 m as our initial estimate.

name: Lane Centering - Tractor
desc:
The SDT shall be designed to limit the duration of any point on the tractor extent (excluding mirrors) being outside of the centering bounds to a maximum of 5 consecutive seconds WHEN
Clearly defined lane markings are present on both sides of the SDT AND
Lane width is greater than or equal to 4 m AND
Lane horizontal radius of curvature is greater than or equal to 450 m AND
No actor within lateral consideration zone with relative lateral distance less than or equal to the Safe Lateral Buffer (0.3m).
rationale:
Rationale:
 
Excluding mirrors because, it will tighten the wandering space if we include the mirrors and may also impact oscillation of SDT to maintain the bounds. Also not a priority from product stand point.
Horizontal radius of curvatures below 450 meters is not considered because it's the min. on Crawl ODD.
Lane width greater than 4 meters excluded although the ODD says maximum Lane width of 6 meters , cause it could mean a merge or gore area where SDT enters into another behavior and also we may not want to get into center of Exiting lane/ Merging lane.
      
5 seconds for acceptable violation is an initial estimate.

name: Lane Centering - Trailer
desc:
The SDT shall be designed to limit the duration of any point on the trailer extent being outside of the centering bounds to a maximum of 5 consecutive seconds WHEN
Clearly defined lane markings are present on both sides of the SDT AND
Lane width is greater than or equal to 4 m AND
Lane horizontal radius of curvature is greater than or equal to 450 m AND
No actor within lateral consideration zone with relative lateral distance less than or equal to the Safe Lateral Buffer (0.3m).

name: Drive at or below the Legal Speed Limit
desc:
The SDT shall be designed to drive at or below the legal speed limit.
 
Note: The Legal speed limit is the maximum permissible road speed from traffic signs.
rationale: The SDT shall follow the speed limit

name: Maintain Distance Greater than or Equal to Lateral Safety Distance to OMVs
desc:
The SDT shall be designed to maintain a distance greater than or equal to the lateral safety distance to all OMVs within the lateral consideration zone, 
 
WHEN, 
(clearly defined lane markings are present AND the distance to the outside lane boundary is more than 0.3 m) OR
The lateral distance to other OMVs in the lateral consideration zone is more than the (lateral safety distance + 0.15 m)
rationale:
So that the SDT maintains a safe distance to the adjacent OMVs reducing the safety risk of near-misses or collisions.
 
The SDT shall not drive close to the lane boundary or leave the ego lane for maintain the distance (0.3 m for now)  

 
 
 
In case there is a vehicle on the opposite side, the SDT shall not violate when the distance to this vehicle. The buffer is given to allow inaccuracies in the subsystems and behavior

name: Maintain Distance Greater than Absolute Minimum Lateral Distance to OMV
desc: The SDT shall be designed to maintain a lateral distance greater than 0 m to OMVs in the lateral consideration zone ​​​.

name: Maintain Distance Greater than Absolute Minimum Longitudinal Distance to OMV
desc: The SDT shall maintain a longitudinal distance greater than 0 m to OMVs in front of the SDT

name: Maintain Distance Greater than Safe Lateral Buffer to OMVs
desc: The SDT shall be designed to maintain a lateral distance greater than or equal to 0.3 m to OMVs in the lateral consideration zone.

name: Lane change maneuver
desc:
Lane change maneuver is achieved with the following steps.
Communicate : The SDT indicates its intention to make a lane change by signaling and biasing (inside its own lane) to the direction of the intended lane change
Execution: The SDT starts to laterally move to the target lane by crossing the lane boundary.
Cancel: The SDT looks for a new gap by continuing driving in its own lane. The SDT is still in its own lane and lane change execution has not started.
Completion: The complete tractor and trailer body is in target lane and the SDT adjusted its longitudinal and lateral position in target lane. Turn indicator is turned off.
Abort: The SDT has started to move laterally onto target lane and has not completely finished the lateral movement. The SDT decides to move back to the original lane and continue driving on its own lane.
 

 
The above diagram is to illustrate different functional blocks needed for a lane change maneuver. Based on the scenario, few of the functional blocks are needed to complete the behavior.
This framework will be used for all scenarios where a lane change is needed by the SDT.
tags: Behavior, Driver-Out, Highway - Lane changes / overtaking

name: Start signaling lane change intention
desc:
The SDT shall be designed to
Action: activate its visual indication for lane change in the direction of the lane change
Condition: at least 3 sec before the start of lane change manuever
tags: Behavior, Driver-Out, Highway - Lane changes / overtaking
rationale:
By various law it is needed to show the intention of lane change to other actors sufficiently ahead of the actual lane change manuever.
Texas law : https://law.justia.com/codes/texas/transportation-code/title-7/subtitle-c/chapter-545/subchapter-c/section-545-104/

name: Stop signaling lane change, completion
desc:
The SDT shall be designed to
Action:  deactivate its visual signaling to change lane
Condition: when all parts of the SDT (including mirrors) are inside the interior lane markings of the target lane.
tags: Behavior, Driver-Out, Highway - Lane changes / overtaking
rationale: So that the other road users are aware of the intention of SDT that the lane change maneuver is completed.

name: Stop signaling lane change intention, Aborted
desc:
The SDT shall be designed to
Action: deactivate its visual signaling to change lane
Condition: when all points of the SDT (including the mirrors) are inside the interior lane markings of the original lane.
tags: Behavior, Driver-Out, Highway - Lane changes / overtaking
rationale:
So that, other road users are not confused, as the SDT has no intent to perform the lane change anymore.
The use case ends when the SDT stops signaling its intention due to cancellation/aborting reason.

name: Stop signaling lane change intention, Time Out
desc:
The SDT shall be designed to
Action: deactivate its visual signaling for lane change
Condition: when
1) all points of the SDT are inside the interior lane markings of the original lane, and
2) The visual signal is activated for more than 15 sec
tags: Behavior, Driver-Out, Highway - Lane changes / overtaking
rationale: So that, the SDT does not tries to make a lane change for extended period of time which could confuse other road users.

name: Adjust lateral position, complete lane change
desc:
The SDT shall be designed to
Action: adjust its lateral position to be completely in the SDT's target lane within the 15 sec of the start of the lateral maneuvers.
Condition: when
1. The SDT has lane change visual signal activated, AND
2. The SDT maintains at least the minimum distance to adjacent OMVs.
tags: Behavior, Driver-Out, Highway - Lane changes / overtaking
rationale: SPI on Minimum lateral safe distance: https://torc.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SAFETY/pages/2575499463/draft+Lateral+Safety+Distance

name: Adjust lateral position, abort lane change
desc:
The SDT shall be designed to
Action: adjust its lateral position to be completely in the SDT's original lane
Condition: when
- (a) The SDT is signaling its intention to change lane AND
- (b) More than 0% of the Tractor is already in the SDT's target lane interior lane markings,
tags: Behavior, Driver-Out, Highway - Lane changes / overtaking

name: Adjust longitudinal position - Complete Lane Change
desc:
The SDT shall be designed to 
Action: adjust its longitudinal position to maintain forward TTC of more than 4 sec with the lead vehicles in both original lane and target lane.
Conditions: when
- (a) Lateral Maneuver to change lane has started, AND
- (b) possible sufficient GAP is available
tags: Behavior, Driver-Out, Highway - Lane changes / overtaking
rationale:
From Forward TTC SPI:  https://torcrobotics.jamacloud.com/perspective.req#/items/2907647?projectId=56
 
 
So that, the SDT can position itself correctly in the gap before the start of the lateral maneuver to the target lane.

name: Sufficient gap (Version I- Distance Based)
desc:
The gap between lag OMV and lead OMV (dgap) is sufficient if it is greater than the sum of the minimum distance to lag OMV (dlag,min), the length of SDT (dSDT) and the minimum distance to lead OMV (dlead,min).
 
For lag OMV, the gap is calculated from rear of SDT to front bumper of lag OMV. and for lead OMV, the gap is calculated from the front bumper of SDT to rear of lead OMVs.
 
The current gap (d0,gap) is calculated based on the current positions (P0,SDT, P0,lag, P0,lead), velocities (v0,SDT, v0,lag, v0,lead) and accelerations (a0,SDT, a0,lag, a0,lead) of SDT, lag OMV and lead OMV (respectively).
 
The predicted gap (d1,gap) is calculated based on the predicted positions (P1,SDT, P1,lag, P1,lead), predicted velocities (v1,SDT, v1,lag, v1,lead) and predicted accelerations (a1,SDT, a1,lag, a1,lead) of SDT, lag OMV and lead OMV (respectively).
 
The gap is predicted for future.The selection/design of prediction function is up to system design based on feasibility and prediction error.
 

 
 
The Minimum distance to lag OMV (dlag,min) = (Lane Change distance by Lag OMV (Distance travelled by the Lag OMV before the SDT enters the target lane) + Lag OMV Reaction Distance + Lag OMV Stop Distance + Standoff Distance to Lag OMV ) - (Lane change Distance by SDT (Distance travelled by the SDT before the SDT enters the target lane) + SDT Stop Distance)
 





 
 
 
 
 
vSDT = Longitudinal Speed of the SDT
 
bSDT = Deceleration of the SDT = 4.5 m/s2 (TBR)
 
dy = Lateral distance the SDT including mirrors needs to travel to reach inner edge of lane boundary = 0.30 m (TBR)
 
alatSDT = Lateral Acceleration of the SDT = 1 m/s2 (TBR)
 
vOMVLag = Longitudinal speed of the OMV
 
 
tresponseOMVLag = Response time of lag OMV = 1,2 s (TBR)
 
 
aOMVLagMax = Maximum Acceleration of lag OMV during the response time = 1 m/s2 (TBR)
 
Standoff Distance to Lag OMV is equal to 10 m(TBR)
 
The below parameters are for Over speeding  OMVs 
If longitudinal velocity of Lag OMV is equal to or less than 30 m/s(TBR)
bOMVLag = Deceleration of Lag OMV is equal to 3.0 m/s2(TBR)
If longitudinal velocity of Lag OMV is between 30 m/s(TBR) and 45 m/s(TBR)
bOMVLag = Deceleration of Lag OMV is between 3.0 m/s2(TBR) and 5.0 m/s2(TBR) (respectively). The intermediate values are calculated by means of linear interpolation method. The resolution is 0.5 m/s (TBR) for interpolation.

If longitudinal velocity of Lag OMV is equal to or greater than 45 m/s(TBR)
bOMVLag = Deceleration of Lag OMV is equal to 5.0 m/s2(TBR)
 
 
The Minimum distance to lead OMV (dlead,min) = (Lane Change distance by SDT (Distance travelled by the SDT before the SDT enters the target lane) + SDT Reaction Distance + SDT Stop Distance + Standoff Distance to Lead OMV ) - (Lane change Distance by Lead OMV (Distance travelled by the Lead OMV before the SDT enters the target lane) + Lead OMV Stop Distance)
 
(SDT Stop Distance + Lane change Distance by SDT + SDT Reaction Distance + Standoff Distance to Lead OMV ) 
- (Lead OMV Stop Distance + Lane change Distance by Lead OMV)
 




 
 

 
vSDT = Longitudinal Speed of the SDT
 
bSDT = Deceleration of the SDT = 4.5 m/s2 (TBR)
 
dy = Lateral distance the SDT including mirrors needs to travel to reach inner edge of lane boundary = 0.30 m (TBR)
 
alatSDT = Lateral Acceleration of the SDT = 1 m/s2 (TBR)
 
vOMVLead = Longitudinal speed of the Lead OMV
 
tresponseSDT = Response time of SDT = 1.2 s (TBR)
 
aSDTMax = Maximum Acceleration of SDT during the response time = 1 m/s2 (TBR)
 
bOMVLead = Deceleration of Lead OMV = 7.0 m/s2 (TBR)
 
Standoff Distance to Lead OMV is equal to 10 m(TBR)
tags: Behavior, Driver-Out, Highway - Lane changes / overtaking
rationale:
The analysis of defining the threshold for large gap can be found in the below link.
https://torc.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/VD/pages/1028784268/Target+gap+for+lane+change+entering+to+highway+and+exit+from+highway
 
 
3 m/s2 as deceleration limit for lag OMV is chosen based on recommendation from ALKS standard.

name: Sufficient Gap (version II- Time-Based)
desc:
The SDT shall maintain at least (Range_Rear / Speed_Rear) = 1 sec from the rear vehicle, and (Range_Lead / Speed_Ego) = 1.5 sec from the lead vehicle once at least one point of the SDT is inside the interior lane markings of the target vehicle until the lane change is completed or aborted.
 
for Stationary Situations, the gap is distance based (Version I) rather than time based gap.
rationale: this is from the framing from the Product KPIs.

name: Maximum duration of lateral maneuver for Lane Change
desc: Maximum duration of lateral maneuver for Lane Change is 15 sec.
tags: Behavior, Driver-Out, Highway - Lane changes / overtaking
rationale: So that it aligns with the KPI from Product.

name: Lane Change Completed Success Rate
desc:
A lane change is successfully completed when:
1. Lane Change signal is activated at least 3 sec before the start of the lateral maneuver, AND
2. All points of the SDT is completely inside the target lane within the Maximum duration of lateral maneuver for Lane Change AND
3. The lane change signal has deactivated once the SDT is completely inside the target lane.
 
Lane Change Success rate = (Successful Completed Lane Change / Total Maneuver Attempts) * 100 
 
Total maneuver attempts include:
1. Aborted Lane Change maneuvers, AND
2. Canceled Lane Change maneuvers, AND
3. Lane Change that takes more than 15 sec of lateral maneuver, AND
4. Lane Changes with failed signal activation/deactivation, AND
5. Successful completed Lane Change maneuvers
tags: Behavior, Driver-Out, Highway - Lane changes / overtaking

name: Lane Change Aborted Success Rate
desc:
Aborted Lane Change is successful when
1. The SDT returns to its lane of origin within the Maximum duration of lateral maneuver for Lane Change, AND
2. Deactivates its signal after all the SDT points are inside the interior lane markings of the original lane
 
Lane Change Abort Rate = (Aborted Maneuvers / Total Maneuver Attempts) * 100
 
Total maneuver attempts include:
1. Aborted Lane Change maneuvers, AND
2. Canceled Lane Change maneuvers, AND
3. Lane Change that takes more than 15 sec of lateral maneuver, AND
4. Lane Changes with failed signal activation/deactivation, AND
5. Successful completed Lane Change maneuvers
tags: Behavior, Driver-Out, Highway - Lane changes / overtaking

name: Harsh Brake Occurrence Rate for Lane Change maneuvers
desc:
The SDT shall have less than 2(TBD) harsh brake events over 2000 miles, while performing lane change related maneuvers.
 
harsh braking thresholds are determined based on the SPI.
rationale: SPI link for harsh brake events: https://torc.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SAFETY/pages/2571141387/draft+Hard+Braking

name: Drive at or above Minimum Highway Speed
desc:
The SDT shall be designed to drive at or above the limit defined through the minimum of 
road curvature speed
rollover speed
legal speed 
average traffic speed 
minus 10 m/s
 
WHEN
SDT is on a highway AND
no speed limit sign with a lower speed limit than the current within 300 m in front of the SDT AND
no vehicle within 5 seconds distance to the front in the ego lane.
rationale: So that SDT can drive with a lower speed than what is defined by the maximum highway speed but still make progress towards the mission.

name: Drive at or below Geometric maximum speed
desc:
The SDT shall be designed to drive below the maximum geometric speed limit, 
 
WHEN
The SDT drives on the highway
 
 
Note: 
The maximum geometric speed limit is defined by 
 
 
V_geometry = SQRT(g*R*(e+f-0.15*G)), where
'g' is the gravitational acceleration (m/s^2), 'R' is the horizontal radius of curvature (m), 'e' is the superelevation, 'f' is the side friction factor, 'G' is the road grade (%, positive for uphill, negative for downhill) and 0.15 is the grade adjustment coefficient.
The friction factor 'f' decreases with speed, and is defined empirically as f = 0.17 -0.00143*V. At low speeds (~30 mph), f ~ 0.13 and at high speeds(~80 mph), f ~ 0.06. It's bounded between 0.07 and 0.17.

name: Drive at or below rollover speed
desc:
The SDT shall be designed to drive below the rollover speed 
 
When
The SDT drives on a highway
 
Note: The rollover speed is defined as
V_rollover =  SQRT(g*R*t/(2*h)), where 'g' is the gravitational acceleration (m/s^2), 'R' is the horizontal radius of curvature (m), 't' is the truck axle width (m), 'h' is the center of gravity height (m).

Average traffic speed = average (average rear vehicle speed with 5 sec (TBR) headway from the SDT, median speed of adjacent vehicle in the consideration zone with maximum headway of 5 sec (TBR) away from the SDT).

name: Maximum Lateral Acceleration for Highway Driving
desc:
The SDT shall be designed to apply a lateral acceleration less than or equal to a_lat_max = MIN(a_lat_geometry, a_lat_rollover), where
 
a_lat_geometry = V_geometry^2/R = g*(e + f -0.15*G)
 
where, 'g' is the gravitational acceleration (m/s^2), 'e' is the superelevation, 'f' is the side friction factor, 'G' is the road grade (%, positive for uphill, negative for downhill) and 0.15 is the grade adjustment coefficient.
 
and,
 
a_lat_rollover = V_rollover^2/R = g*t/(2*h)
 
where,  'g' is the gravitational acceleration (m/s^2), 'R' is the horizontal radius of curvature (m), 't' is the truck axle width (m), 'h' is the center of gravity height (m).
rationale:
So that the SDT maintains its dynamic stability and does not slide or roll over.

name: Activate Hazard Light
desc:
The SDT shall be designed to have active Hazard Light
 
WHEN
the long velocity is below 1 m/s AND
no lead vehicle within 15 m (TBD) AND
is on a Highway
rationale: Necessary to have hazard lights activated on the Highway when Stop in Lane executed to standstill

name: Definition: Interior Lane Boundary
desc:
Interior Lane Boundary is defined as an unbroken (continuous) curve lying along the surface of a road.
The curve defining the interior Lane Boundary is always constructed such that the curve intersects two or more reference points from a set of visible lane markings on the road surface.
For interior lane boundary, the Lane Marking reference point is located at the point on the Lane Marking closest to the inner edge of the lane that the Lane Boundary is a part of.
For Dashed or Dotted Painted Lane markings, a reference point is at minimum at the start and end of the paint for the discrete marking.

name: Definition: Exterior Lane Boundary
desc:
Exterior Lane Boundary is defined as an unbroken (continuous) curve lying along the surface of a road.
The curve defining the exterior Lane Boundary is always constructed such that the curve intersects two or more reference points from a set of visible lane markings on the road surface.
For exterior lane boundary, the Lane Marking reference points** is located at the point on the Lane Marking farthest to the inner edge of the lane that the Lane Boundary is a part of.
For Dashed or Dotted Painted Lane markings, a reference point is at minimum at the start and end of the paint for the discrete marking.

name: Definition: Centering Bound
desc:
The Centering Bound defines a "Virtual Lane" within the SDT's travel lane. The SDT must maintain all physical points of the tractor body (excluding mirrors) and all points of the trailer within this virtual lane. These bounds are calculated to ensure the vehicle remains centered while accounting for both human like driving behavior and the physics of trailer off-tracking.

rationale:
Used a previously done analysis for these calculations, a simple explanation is below, for a truck width of 2.585m:
 
The Human driving baseline for wandering distance (d)
We use a Normal Distribution model of human steering wander (Standard Deviation of 0.254m)
For a 3.5m lane, we set the distribution at 50%. Solving the integral of the normal distribution gives a wandering distance (d) of 0.3426m.
For a 4.0m lane, we increase this to 60% (allowing more wander in wider lanes), resulting in (d) of 0.4300m.
Note: The 50% "wheel wander" standard deviation, represents 50% of observed human driving,
 
The Physical Boundary (Distance from Lane Boundary)
We calculate the "Keep Out Buffer" zone from the lane lines using this formula:
Distance from Lane Boundary = (Lane Width - (SDT width + d))/2.
 
Curvature compensation (ROC)
As the road curves, the trailer off-track (cuts the corners). To prevent the trailer from crossing the lane line, we must allow the wandering distance (d) to increase. So, for every 250m decrease in ROC, we increase the allowed wandering space by 0.0084m (for 3.5m lanes) to account for the physical swing of the trailer. This ensures the trailer stays inside the bounds even when the tractor is centered.
 
The 0.0084m value is derived from the AASHTO (Greenbook) "Simplified Off-tracking" formula, which uses a linear approximation (Off Tracking = (L_eff^2) / (2 * ROC)) to calculate how much a standard trailer cuts a corner. Here we used L effective wheelbase of trailer as 13m (53ft). 
 
For more detailed reasoning, please review the analysis in,
 Link to Analysis: 
1.  https://torc.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/VD/pages/730005794/Rationale+for+Lane+Centering+-+General
 
2. https://torc.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/VD/pages/716475219/Update+the+centering+zone+width+based+on+inputs+from+data+analysis
 
Methodology behind the calculations in the, "Autonomous vehicles wheel wander: Structural impact on flexible pavements" paper.

name: Definition: Lateral Consideration Zone
desc:
The lateral consideration zone shall be the area directly adjacent to the SDT Tractor and Trailer on the left and right side, starting longitudinally 0.3 m ahead of the front Bumper and ending 0.3 m behind the Trailer or, when no trailer is attached, behind the end of the Tractor. 
The lateral consideration zone shall laterally extend 4 m from the outside edge of the Tractor and Trailer extent.

desc:
Clearly defined lane markings satisfy the following:
Width 4-8 inches

name: Definition: Average Traffic Speed
desc:
The Average traffic speed is the minimum of
the current AND
the averaged over the last 2 min 
of the velocity of traffic in existing direct adjacent left and right lanes of the ego vehicle, which follows within the next 2 mi along the defined route.

name: Maximum Allowed Duration for Lane Departure Event - Tractor
desc: The SDT shall be designed to limit the violations of  Stay in Lane - Tractor to be less than 10 sec per event.
rationale: For Driver Out, SDT needs to drive within lane 99% of the total driving time (assuming 100% robotic). Since this accounts to almost 7hrs of driving, SDT can have cumulative lane departure duration of total 4.2 minutes or 252 seconds. Assuming we could have a maximum of 25 unintended lane departure events, the average duration of a single event to be ~10 seconds.

name: Maximum Allowed Duration for Lane Departure Event - Trailer
desc: The SDT shall be designed to limit the violations of  Stay In Lane - Trailer to be less than 10 sec per event.
rationale: For Driver Out, SDT needs to drive within lane 99% of the total driving time (assuming 100% robotic). Since this accounts to almost 7hrs of driving, SDT can have cumulative lane departure duration of total 4.2 minutes or 252 seconds. Assuming we could have a maximum of 25 unintended lane departure events, the average duration of a single event to be ~10 seconds.

name: Centering Bound Acceptable Violation
desc:
The SDT shall be designed to have an acceptable violation of centering bounds WHEN
1. Any part of the SDT (trailer and tractor, excluding mirrors) stays outside of the centering bound for less than 2 sec (TBR), AND
2. The time between two consecutive violations of less than 2 sec from centering bound is more than 30 sec.
rationale:
So that exiting the centering zone is acceptable (because centering is subjective and not the highest priority requirement) as long as the SDT is violating it for very short amount of time with small amplitude in a way that does not cause any severe weaving issues.
 
Rationale for less than 2 seconds: Kinematic equation with smooth lateral acceleration of 0.5 m/s^2 and 15 cm of distance: 0.5*0.5*t^2 = 0.15 --> t = 0.78 sec --> 2t = 1.6 (1*t for 15 cm out of centering bound, 1*t for 15 cm back to the centering bound) --> 15 cm comes from the Motion Control analysis on amplitude and frequency of severe weaving (Lane Keeping : Framework for Requirements - Virtual Driver - Confluence (atlassian.net)) 
 
In simple terms, we want the SDT to drive like a professional human, not a rigid robot. Humans occasionally drift slightly when there's a heavy crosswind or a bump in the road.
We allow the SDT 2 seconds to fix a minor drift because a slow, smooth correction is safer for the trailer than a sudden, sharp jerk. However, to make sure the truck isn't weaving down the highway, we require the SDT to drive within the centering bounds for at least 30 seconds before we can forgive another violation. This ensures the ride is stable, comfortable, and safe for everyone on the road.

name: Maximum Lateral Jerk for Highway Driving
desc:
The SDT shall be designed to have a maximum lateral jerk less than or equal to j_lat_max = MIN(j_lat_geometry, j_lat_rollover), where
 
j_lat_geometry = g*(e + f -0.15*G)/T
 
where, 'g' is the gravitational acceleration (m/s^2), 'e' is the superelevation, 'f' is the side friction factor, 'G' is the road grade (%, positive for uphill, negative for downhill), 0.15 is the grade adjustment coefficient and T is the transition time in seconds. T is the time duration over which a vehicle transitions from zero lateral acceleration (straight driving) to the full steady-state lateral acceleration when entering a curve. 
 
and,
 
j_lat_rollover = g*t/(2*h)/T
 
where,  'g' is the gravitational acceleration (m/s^2), 't' is the truck axle width (m), 'h' is the center of gravity height (m), and T is the transition time in seconds.
rationale:
So that the SDT maintains its dynamic stability and does not slide or roll over.
 
Results based on AASTHO combinations of radius of curvature, superelevation, road grade, and design speeds.

name: Lateral Safety Distance Violation Rate
desc: The SDT shall be designed to have an occurrence rate of less than 0.03 events per mile for events where SDT violates the lateral safety distance.
rationale: For Driver Out, SDT needs maintain a distance greater than the lateral safety distance to OMVs at least 99.9% of the total driving time (assuming 100% robotic). Since this accounts to almost 7hrs of driving, SDT can have cumulative lateral safety distance violation time of total 25.2 seconds. Assuming we could have a maximum of 12 events of ~2 seconds each.
